rounds.response: Do not treat idempotency_key + final event as an absolute uniqueness guarantee—use it as the primary dedupe key for normal auto-apply logic, but keep defensive checks because delivery is at-least-once and cross-system divergences can occur. Minimal required checks: verify idempotency_key scope (order/txn), confirm payload checksum/timestamp matches any previously-applied final, validate against the canonical payment ledger (amount/status), and detect unexpected ordering (e.g., compensating after final). Auto-apply rule: if idempotency_key unseen → apply final; if seen with identical final payload → no-op; if seen with differing payload or conflict with ledger → do NOT auto-apply and escalate for manual reconciliation. For anomalous sequences (duplicate/differing finals, missing compensations, finals after release) tooling must alert the Checkout On‑Call (configured PagerDuty service) and open the Jira per the runbook. Finally, instrument metrics (duplicate-final rate, reconciliation queue size, time-to-resolution) and set thresholds so SRE can detect systemic problems rather than only per-order noise.
